correctness.rationale: From the full RESULT.md proof: if singleton {x} mapped to universal target c, back yields two source sets through x mapped to incompatible leaves a,b, contradicting forth. Hence singleton leaf colors q(x). If f(A)=leaf a, every element has color a by forth; if A contains both colors it must map to c. If A monochromatic a but f(A)=c, back yields an intersecting b-leaf image, impossible. Thus f(A)=q[A]; back forces both colors, and every surjective q satisfies forth/back by explicit ≤2-element lifting. No choice is assumed for infinite X, and direct image is left adjoint of inverse image. n finite count 2^n-2, infinite count 2^|X|. Inspected verify.cpp enumerates all maps for n≤4, but the arbitrary-X theorem is proved symbolically; the census was not independently rerun.
